# Artifact Qualification Protocol v1

Status: **RATIFIED_ACTIVE_MANDATORY**

This protocol governs consumer-facing interactive visual artifacts, page/showroom rebuilds, carousel or spatial interaction instruments, and comparable artifact projects assigned to any room.

## Chain of command

1. Assignment and scope.
2. Existing-construct and authority discovery.
3. Architectural adoption and preservation before reconstruction.
4. Artifact construction.
5. Verifier qualification.
6. Exact-head real-browser qualification.
7. Page Excellence architecture.
8. Page Excellence implementation.
9. Responsive, accessibility, and reduced-motion qualification.
10. Reference-Class / Awards qualification.
11. All applicable integrated repository gates.
12. Consumer-rendered inspection occurrence.
13. Owner visual/product acceptance.
14. Promotion authority.

## Failure law

Any failure must first be classified as verifier, artifact, or infrastructure failure. The repair must target the actual defective layer. Any candidate mutation invalidates prior PASS evidence for promotion purposes and requires qualification again on the new exact head.

A required browser interaction may not be replaced with synthetic DOM success. A PR, commit, source file, raw HTML file, screenshot, or workflow receipt may not substitute for a functioning consumer-rendered inspection occurrence.

Technical PASS does not equal owner product acceptance. Owner acceptance is mandatory before promotion to the production branch.

## Reference case

PR #998, Methods and Models rotational text instrument, is the empirical reference case for this protocol. Exact candidate `9568f1f5f2e4047e7d422f9a49cf133d6e6e31b1` passed all attached workflows after verifier, artifact, compatibility, and infrastructure defects were separately classified, repaired, and requalified.

The procedure is ratified from that evidence. The PR #998 product itself remains held pending consumer-rendered owner inspection and therefore has no visual/product acceptance or promotion authority from this ratification.
